newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman LNG Co expects to secure more gas sales soon.
newsitem.headline: Oman LNG Co expects to secure more gas sales soon.

text.p: Oman expects to soon secure sales of up to 2.5 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) a year for export between 2000 and 2003, an oil official said.
"In the coming months we expect to finalise arrangements for sales of our short-term capacity," Oman LNG Co marketing and shipping vice president Ian Coult told Reuters.
Oman LNG has 2.5 million tonnes of LNG from its liquefaction plant available for the years 2001 and 2002.
Oman is setting up a $6 billion project to produce 6.6 million tonnes a year of LNG from the first quarter of 2000.
In April Oman LNG Co signed heads of agreement for the 25-year supply of four million tonnes of LNG to Korea Gas Corp from the year 2000.
Last month state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) signed an agreement to buy up to 2.2 million tonnes of Omani LNG each year for 25 years with deliveries starting in 2003.
Oman LNG Co now wants to secure sales to cover the delay in liftings between its Korean and Thai customers.
"We are talking to a number of potential buyers. The LNG world is not a huge place. There are several buyers in Japan, one in Thailand, one in Turkey and of course Korea," Coult said.
"We know Korea still has unmet demand in the period 2000 to 2003 and we are very keen to confirm sales."
"There is a lot of Korean demand, there is more uncertainty in places like Japan and Taiwan," he added.
Oman LNG Co is 51 percent owned by the Oman government with the rest of the equity split between foreign firms.

Royal Dutch Shell Group unit Shell Overseas Trading Ltd owns 34 percent, Total SA owns six percent, Partex (Oman) Corp has two percent, Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsui and Co Ltd each hold three percent and Itochu Corp has one percent.
Last week a government official said Oman aims to finalise a $2.25 billion financing package for the downstream part of the project by the end of the month.

This will allow it to sign a firm sales and purchase agreement with Korea Gas Corp and clear the way for Oman LNG to sign a $1.2 billion contract with Japan's Chiyoda Corp and Foster Wheeler Corp of the United States to build the liquefaction plant at al-Ghalilah.
